concepts.name: Big-O notation

concepts.name: Polynomials

concepts.name: Complex numbers

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a finite alphabet and several one-dimensional tapes, each with its own head moving one cell per step.

concepts.name: Nondegenerate bilinear spaces
concepts.gloss: A vector space with a symmetric bilinear form having no nonzero vector orthogonal to everything, so each nondegenerate subspace U splits the space as U ⊥ U^⊥ with an orthogonal projection P_U.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.

For a nondegenerate rational subspace $U\subset\mathcal F$, write
$P_U$ for the projection onto $U$ along $U^\perp$.

concepts.name: Tensor products
concepts.gloss: The tensor product of vector spaces or linear maps, used to build multidimensional transforms, label spaces F^{⊗3}, and operators acting independently on several coordinates.

evidence.quote:
The ambient label space is $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ with its tensor
bilinear form.

every frame and edge
operator is then the tensor product of its one-column version over
these $k$ coordinates.

concepts.name: Fixed finite-tape machine model and stream operations
concepts.gloss: The model of one machine with a fixed alphabet and fixed number of tapes, where arrays are stored in lexicographic address order and elementary scans (digit moves, row splits, pointwise maps) cost time linear in the logical volume V of stored bits.

evidence.quote:
A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of
one-dimensional tapes.
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.

Each of the following operations on an array of
volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes:

concepts.name: Controlled shifts and rational scalings
concepts.gloss: A linear-time stream operation that adds to a later address field an offset computed from earlier fields, or multiplies it by a fixed rational unit, modulo q^b, by splitting and re-merging blocks.

evidence.quote:
The next operations are linear because their target field follows their
control fields.

Multiplication of $y$ by any of the specified rational units, and its
inverse, also costs $O(V)$.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The normalized transform (F_q u)_k = (1/q) Σ_j u_j e^{−2πijk/q} and its opposite-sign inverse F_q^+, contractions for the max norm, applied axis by axis on multidimensional arrays.

evidence.quote:
Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction, since each
output averages inputs multiplied by complex numbers of modulus one.

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product in ℂ[x]/(x^S − 1): coefficient lists are combined with indices added modulo S, and transforms turn it into pointwise multiplication.

evidence.quote:
let $*$ denote cyclic convolution in the displayed

concepts.name: Multiplication by radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Splitting each n-bit input into radix-2^b digits turns integer multiplication into convolution of short integer coefficient lists followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's 1971 proposal that Θ(n log n) is the optimal order of n-bit integer multiplication on multitape Turing machines; disproving it requires one machine with T(n)/(n lg n) → 0.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

Its negation requires one machine satisfying
$\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$.

concepts.title: The $n\log n$ optimality conjecture

symbols.name: logarithm

concepts.name: Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplier
concepts.gloss: The 2021 deterministic multitape algorithm multiplying N-bit integers in O(N log N) time via Gaussian resampling and Nussbaumer polynomial transforms; here it is both the base of the reduction and an ordinary subroutine.

evidence.quote:
Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper

Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine
calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadic fixed-point arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Exact arithmetic on complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators, stored as signed fixed-point words on the p-bit disk grid and truncated toward zero by Q_p.

evidence.quote:

let $Q_p$ truncate each real and

concepts.name: Disk-grid approximation and error accounting
concepts.gloss: Each routine approximates a linear contraction on the p-bit disk grid with an error bound in units of 2^−p, and composed errors add because contractions do not amplify input errors.

evidence.quote:
Composing such algorithms
adds their errors: at each step, insert the exact map at the computed
input and use its contraction bound on the accumulated input error.

concepts.name: Normalized butterfly H₀
concepts.gloss: The two-point map H₀(u, v) = ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2), the radix-two step of a Fourier transform, applied coefficientwise to polynomial records.

two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Nussbaumer–Quandalle Fourier transforms over arrays of R_r elements using ω_t = y^{2r/t} as roots of unity, computed by radix-two decimation-in-frequency rounds of butterflies and monomial twiddles, with outputs left in bit-reversed stored frequency order.

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Multiplying two polynomial records of R_r by packing their signed fixed-point coefficients into large integers, calling the O(N log N) integer multiplier, and unpacking the exact product.

evidence.quote:
Signed coefficient
packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

One can compute the exact Gaussian integer

concepts.name: Bank-exchange linear network
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network of wires (roles) and pointwise gates—copy, gather, scatter, side injection on a schedule of eight rows over three stages—that maps two data banks (X, Y) to (−Y, X) while restoring arbitrary initial scratch values.

evidence.quote:
Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two
banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary
value.
A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.
(X_a,Y_a)\longmapsto(-Y_a,X_a)

concepts.name: Three-element subset intersection construction
concepts.gloss: Indexing data by 3-element subsets of a 100-element set so that gather/scatter through central wires yields coefficients depending on |S ∩ T| (mod 2 or minus one), with side wires cancelling unwanted neighbor terms, as in Frankl–Wilson/Alon and index-code decoding.

evidence.quote:
The construction uses
three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending
on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted
coefficients.

Alon's presentation of the
Frankl--Wilson construction

concepts.gloss: Assigning each network vertex an invertible operator D_v on wire arrays so that stored data is D_v g; pointwise gates commute with a common frame, so a route from role w to ρ(w) applies only D_sink D_source^{−1} and intermediate frames cancel.

evidence.quote:

concepts.name: Subspace labels and orthogonal residuals
concepts.gloss: Nested nondegenerate subspaces of the m-dimensional space F^{⊗3} attached to gates and terminals; on each edge the orthogonal residual's dimension counts the smaller operations needed for that edge's frame change.

evidence.quote: The subspaces at adjacent vertices are nested.

the
\emph{orthogonal residual} is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside
the larger one

concepts.name: Rank saving s < Wm
concepts.gloss: The decisive inequality that the total number s of smaller calls over all edges (sum of residual dimensions or ranks) is strictly less than the wire count W times the label dimension m.

evidence.quote:
The decisive property is that the total
number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.title: Rank saving $s<Wm$

symbols.name: smaller call count

symbols.name: label dimension

concepts.name: Volume-normalized recursion
concepts.gloss: Splitting rows cyclically among W roles makes each of s child calls act on volume V/W, so cost per bit obeys F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k−1} + O(1), and s/W < m^τ yields a power saving e^τ in the parameter.

evidence.quote:
A recursive call at parameter $mf$ therefore uses $s$ calls at parameter
$f$, each on a stream of volume $V/W$.

This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Address shears (H, D) ↦ (H + MD, D)
concepts.gloss: Array permutations Φ_M that add a rational matrix M times one address-field vector D to another H modulo q^b; the bit network's rational matrix interface makes the endpoint operator the shear H ← H + D on every role.

evidence.quote: For the bit procedure, that endpoint operator is an address shear:

For a matrix $M$, the frame $\Phi_M$ moves the array entry
at $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$

concepts.name: Lower triangular (Bruhat) factorization
concepts.gloss: Writing a rank-a rational matrix as E₁ Π E₂ with invertible lower triangular E₁, E₂ and a partial permutation Π with a ones, so a matrix shear costs a field interchanges plus linear-time triangular updates.

concepts.name: Fast address-chunk interchange in O(V u^τ)
concepts.gloss: The first tape procedure: exchanging two disjoint u-bit address fields of a stored array in O(V u^τ) time, τ = 1 − 2^−50, by recursively applying the bit network with XOR gates and row splits, rather than by data movement alone.

evidence.quote: Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

Although its final effect is an exact permutation, its intermediate
steps form pointwise XOR combinations of data.

concepts.title: Fast address-chunk interchange in $O(Vu^\tau)$

concepts.name: Binary phase frames
concepts.gloss: The complex network's frames 𝒞_U = H^{⊗m} diag(i^{wt(P_U x) mod 4}) H^{⊗m} for binary labels U, whose edge changes factor into one two-point kernel C = aI + bX per orthonormal residual vector and telescope to C^{⊗m} on every role.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: A tape operation XORing the selected bits of one address chunk into the corresponding bits of another, using a temporary chunk, whole-chunk cyclic shifts and a sorted correction of a small explicit exceptional set.

evidence.quote:
We implement a binary row addition on corresponding selected bits in two
address chunks.

Those changes are implemented by whole-chunk moves and
controlled shifts, followed by a deterministic correction of the
explicitly identified exceptional addresses.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer in O(V d^λ′)
concepts.gloss: The second tape procedure: applying H₀ on the same bit of up to d address chunks at once in O(V d^λ′) time, λ′ < 1, by recursing through the complex phase network, then converting C^{⊗D} to H₀^{⊗D} with diagonal phases and a dyadic scale before one final truncation.

evidence.quote:
one selects the same bit position in each of at most $d$
equal-width address chunks, and the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a
fixed $\lambda'<1$.

A single
truncation follows the completed contractive layer.

concepts.name: Synthetic transform tape layout and cost
concepts.gloss: Arranging the axes of a multidimensional synthetic transform so that each round's selected bits sit at a common offset in K-bit chunks, letting simultaneous butterfly layers and chunk interchanges compute every round.

evidence.quote:
To apply Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} in a transform round,
we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common
offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

concepts.name: Normalized convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Computing the normalized cyclic convolution of R_r-valued arrays by two forward synthetic transforms kept in their stored frequency order, pointwise signed-packed polynomial products, and the opposite transform consuming that order.

evidence.quote:
The two forward synthetic transforms
retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product, and
the opposite transform consumes that order.

concepts.name: Coefficient phase twist
concepts.gloss: The isomorphism x_d ↦ ζy (ζ = e^{πi/r}) turning cyclic convolution along the last axis into negacyclic multiplication in ℂ[y]/(y^r+1), whose negative wrap reproduces the cyclic wrap after untwisting.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic
wrap after the twist is removed.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: The Agarwal–Cooley isomorphism x ↦ Π x_i^{μ_i} turning one cyclic convolution of length S = Π s_i (distinct primes s_i near powers of two) into a multidimensional cyclic convolution, implemented on tape by triangular controlled shifts.

evidence.quote:
the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of
distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves
convolution.

Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder
theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic
convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: The Harvey–van der Hoeven identity expressing a Fourier transform of prime length s through one of nearby power-of-two length t, sandwiched between Gaussian-kernel contractions A and B₀ and a power-of-two scale.

evidence.quote:
Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a
power-of-two tensor transform.

concepts.name: Resampling with retained permutations
concepts.gloss: Keeping the source and target coordinate permutations R, Q inside the resampling identity R F_s = 2^γ B₀ Q F_t A rather than sorting, so the target permutation is absorbed by the chirp and the source permutation cancels across forward and inverse transforms in a convolution.

evidence.quote:
Section~\ref{sec:resampling} retains the
source and target coordinate permutations in the transform identity,
so they need not be executed as separate full sorts.

Finally, the source permutation retained during resampling cancels
across the two forward source transforms, their pointwise product,
and the opposite-sign transform.

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Writing a (permuted) Fourier transform as pointwise multiplication by a chirp ā, cyclic convolution with the chirp a, and multiplication by ā again, so the middle power-of-two transform becomes a convolution.

evidence.quote:
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding and carries
concepts.gloss: Removing known normalizations and digit scales, bounding the total coefficient error strictly below 1/2 so rounding recovers the exact integer convolution, then propagating radix-2^b carries to output the 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote:
proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to
obtain the exact binary product.

concepts.name: Parameter choice and cost table
concepts.gloss: The fixed rational exponents (τ = σ = 1 − 2^−50, λ′ = 1 − 2^−54, c = 2^−56, ε = 2^−75, …) and sizes (b = ⌈log₂ n⌉, p = 6b, d = ⌊b^ε⌋) under which every per-bit cost term is at most p^{1−2κ}, giving κ = 2^−182.

evidence.quote:
A compatible choice of rational
parameters makes all terms in its cost table fit Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.gloss: One deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine computes the exact 2n-bit product of two n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) time with κ = 2^−182, via radix digits, a CRT map, Gaussian resampling with retained permutations, Bluestein chirps, a phase twist and synthetic transforms accelerated by fast interchanges and simultaneous butterfly layers, disproving the n log n conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote:
We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers
in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time

The theorem refutes an
eventual $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound for every fixed multiplication
machine in this model.

concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time
